$comment: Every read the infrastructure capture may make. A command that is not here does not run — the capture fails naming it, before anything is sent. Adding one is a change to this file, which is a diff a reviewer sees; that is the whole mechanism. Nothing here may write, restart, migrate, or alter any state, and a reviewer's first question about a new entry should be whether that still holds.

commands.reads: cluster membership, quorum votes and which node is which
every guest and storage the cluster knows about, in one answer
the backup jobs, their schedules and whether each is enabled
the replication jobs, and whether there are any at all
the nodes, their uptime and their coarse load
one node's CPU, memory, root filesystem and running kernel
one node's datastores, their fill and their status
one node's containers and their run state
one node's virtual machines and their run state
one container's declared configuration
one virtual machine's declared configuration
the packages pending on one node, security updates among them
one node's recent task log, including what a failed backup said
failed units, which no API level reports and which is where a silent degradation becomes visible
thin-pool data and metadata percentages, and per-guest volume fill — a datastore threshold cannot make either distinction
the corosync configuration as written, so a missing quorum device or two_node clause is seen rather than inferred
quorum as the cluster stack itself reports it, including a device present in the membership view with no votes
mount state, so a network share that is down is distinguishable from one that is merely quiet
boot history, which is how a kernel installed and never booted is caught
the kernel actually running, against the one installed
the interfaces and bridges that exist, against the ones the configuration names
whether there is any ZFS at all, which decides whether a whole class of detector applies
pending packages as the package manager lists them, for the security subset
